routes.name: R1: disclose at the relay, WOLF reads the mirror, WOLF baits the sentry, tank hit, full clear, then Continue from the cleared save
R2: press at the relay (WOLF refuses), manual bypass, manual mirror port, engineer alone in the lane, missed drop with the coolant cloud, sentry chase and lose, winch re-arm, timed hit, full clear

R3: failures and saves: purge display, Continue from every save (safe point, Records entry, purge, mirror, Records complete, junction A/B/C/D), Pause and all Settings tabs while the line builds (gauge stays at 0.11 in every paused shot), vent knockdown, blast knockdown, WOLF refuses to bait, sentry catch, timed hit, finish
R4 (extra branches): disclose, then the engineer takes the bypass while WOLF is still walking to the contact; drop the tank the moment the panel is reachable while WOLF is still drawing the sentry

gaps: All requested R1, R2 and R3 steps were reached. Final runs logged no driver failures, and all three routes reach the title screen with Continue enabled.

Not reachable in play: WOLF breaking off after a missed drop while he is drawing the sentry ('I'm out. I'll hold at the rubble.'). R4 dropped the tank on the first frame the ARM PANEL answered. The sentry was still patrolling at x=812, 112 px from the mark, and WOLF was at 534, not yet in the lane. The sentry locked onto WOLF while the tank fell (chase speed 230 px/s over the 0.45 s fall) and was hit anyway (R4-049 to R4-052). Once WOLF agrees to draw it, every drop hits.

Not captured: WOLF's 'I'm still checking the drive. Wait for me' line at the mirror. He walks to the mirror as soon as Records loads and was already there whenever the engineer reached it, including after the Continue from the purge save (R3-037/038).
Not captured: a knockdown from the coolant cloud. After a miss the sentry is chasing (R2-051 to R2-054), so it catches the engineer before the 3 s cloud can be reached. No route tried it.

Not captured: knockdowns in the corridor or Records, which have no hazards, and touch or controller layouts (all routes used the keyboard layout; the touch-button labels in the log are the visible on-screen buttons only).

Method: this was driven play, not hands-on play. Godot ran windowed at 1280x720 (no_focus and always-on-top) with --fixed-fps 60, so screenshots do not advance game time. Input went through action presses and button pressed signals from New Game. The driver stops the engineer briefly for each auto-shot, and the timing of the R4 drop depended on turning that off for one walk. A shot is taken 5 frames after any change to the objective card, dialogue, hint, tutorial prompt, visible buttons, overlay, room, knockdown, choice, world flags, line, sentry, arm or WOLF's own moves (16 frames for a knockdown, after any fade has cleared).

Observations from the shots, for whoever analyses the logic: (1) R2-012 and R3-012: after WOLF says no at the breaker, the relay hint still reads 'E: ask WOLF to take the live relay', and he refuses a second time (R2-013). (2) R2-051/052: a miss is announced while the drawn tank sits over the sentry in the cloud; the sentry was 15 px outside the 44 px hit range. (3) R3-041/042: after Continue with both traces copied, the hint at the mirror still says 'E: examine the mirror port.' (4) R1-049/R1-050: the hint says 'Get left of the vent' but the blast zone is x 360-540, and the vent's own range is 250-350. (5) R1-036/R3-051 vs R3-056/057: Continue from junction save A skips WOLF's seam read and starts him at x 56. (6) R3 Pause: the gauge reads 0.11 in every paused and Settings shot (R3-060 to R3-065), so the line is frozen while paused.

Cleanup: the logic-audit/build worktree was removed and the main checkout is clean at e54c338. The scratch game copy with the driver (game/review_capture/routes.gd) and the runner (run_route.sh) remain under logic-audit/. Run logs are in logic-audit/logs/, and each route's raw log is shots/<route>/_log-<route>.json.

problems.title: Hit or miss on the tank drop contradicts what the screen shows
problems.what_player_sees: R2: the drop is called a miss, but in the cloud frame the sentry sits right under the fallen tank, inside the floor-mark brackets: 'The tank hits the floor and vents coolant. The sentry turns on the panel.' R4: the tank is let go while the sentry is still off to the right by the exit-bolt panel, well outside the mark, and it is still a clean 'comes down square and crushes the sentry flat.'
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: This is the core action of the encounter, and what you see works against the result. A sentry that looks covered gets a miss, and a drop that looks early gets a hit. A first-time player can't learn when to press E. WOLF's 'Drop it when it stops' (R1) doesn't help either, because R4 drops before it stops and still wins.
problems.suggestion: Make the hit zone match the floor-mark brackets exactly and show it. Light the mark when the sentry's body is inside it, and draw the tank's falling shadow on the floor. A sentry inside the brackets when the tank lands should always be a hit, and one outside should always be a miss. A drop released while the sentry is still off the mark should not be saved by it chasing WOLF in. If that rescue is kept on purpose, show it with a line like 'WOLF drags it under at the last second.'

problems.title: The ARM PANEL alcove is called safe, but you get spotted and run down inside it
problems.what_player_sees: The hint says 'Get to the ARM PANEL.' Standing at the panel inside its drawn alcove frame then gives 'You're in its lane. Get into the panel alcove or back over the rubble.' In R3 the engineer is still inside the frame when 'The sentry's eyes snap red', and is knocked down there: 'The sentry ran you down in its lane.' In R2, after a miss, the game says 'The ARM PANEL alcove hides you from it' while the sentry is parked in the alcove, over the panel, and the engineer is actually standing back on the rubble.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The game names the alcove as the safe spot and draws a frame around it. Then it tells you you're exposed and kills you inside that frame. The one rule of this encounter (where can I stand?) can't be read from the screen, and the failure looks unfair.
problems.suggestion: Make the alcove's drawn frame the exact safe zone, and keep the sentry's patrol path out of it. Give the safe floor a different tint or stripe. Show 'You're in its lane' only when the engineer is outside the frame. If the safe spot is really 'behind the panel', move the frame and the label to match. Never place the sentry inside the zone the text calls hidden.

problems.title: The rule for the relief vent can't be read: it steams the whole time and 'the gauge' is never shown
problems.what_player_sees: Arming the overload breaker gives 'the relief vent lets go at the top of the gauge' and 'Move off it before the gauge peaks.' A tall steam column is already coming off the vent at the start of the build (gauge about 0.11) and stays there the whole time. The room has several gauges (two dials on the pipes, a dial on the valve, a three-bar meter that counts the valve turns), and none is labelled as the line gauge. The knockdown just says 'The relief vent let go under you.' WOLF stands on the same vent unharmed.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: You're told to watch a gauge you can't find and to avoid a burst that looks like it is already happening. Safe steam and deadly steam look the same, so the knockdown feels random.
problems.suggestion: Add one clearly labelled LINE gauge, for example a vertical bar over the vent that fills and turns red near the top. Keep the vent to a light wisp while the line builds, then give a hard warning (flash or hiss) just before the burst. Have WOLF step off the grate at the warning so the player copies him.

problems.title: 'Get left of the vent' sends you through the active hazard, and the knockdown blames a door that never visibly blew
problems.what_player_sees: SEAL CHARGED gives 'Get left of the vent before the fuse ends.' The engineer is at the valve, and the only way left is across the relief vent, which is still steaming. In the blast knockdown the door is still standing, sealed with orange bars, while the text says 'The door blew with you in front of it.' WOLF, standing next to the engineer, is fine.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The instruction points you into the hazard you were just told to avoid, and it sends you further than needed: per the capture notes, only standing in front of the door is dangerous. When you fail, you never see the cause (no blast, no debris, door intact), so you can't tell how close you came or what hit you.
problems.suggestion: Mark the blast zone on the floor in front of the door, for example hazard stripes that pulse during the fuse. Change the line to 'Get clear of the door' or 'Back off the stripes.' Shut the vent's steam off once the line has peaked so crossing it is clearly safe. On a blast knockdown, show the door blowing and the engineer being thrown before the fade.

problems.title: WOLF says he'll keep clear of the tank while he stands right under it
problems.what_player_sees: 'I'll draw it onto the mark and keep clear of the tank. Drop it when it stops.' WOLF's body is then under the hanging tank, over the floor mark, nose to nose with the sentry. The clamp lets go with WOLF still under it. A moment later the sentry is crushed, and WOLF is fine and walking off.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The dialogue and the picture say opposite things. A player who cares about WOLF will hold off dropping because it looks like the tank will hit him. Then it doesn't, which teaches that the tank only hurts sentries.
problems.suggestion: Have WOLF hold the sentry from just outside the right edge of the mark, with the sentry on the mark between WOLF and the tank. Or have him leap clear as the clamp opens. Then 'keep clear of the tank' matches what you see.

problems.title: After WOLF refuses the relay, the hint still says to ask him, and he answers with a button prompt
problems.what_player_sees: At the breaker WOLF says 'No. I won't take that risk blind. Use the bypass.' At the relay the hint still says 'E: ask WOLF to take the live relay.' Pressing E makes WOLF refuse again: 'I said no. I won't take the live contact. Press E again for the manual bypass.'
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The hint goes against what WOLF just said and pushes the player to badger him. It costs an extra press and makes WOLF look like a menu, not a companion. 'Press E again' is a UI instruction in WOLF's voice. The bypass he mentions is never pointed out or labelled in the room either.
problems.suggestion: Once WOLF has refused, change the relay hint straight away to 'E: take the manual bypass yourself', and label a MANUAL BYPASS lever or handle on the relay. Keep 'Press E' out of WOLF's lines and leave button prompts to the hint bar.

problems.title: The seal 'rises' while it is still there, and the narration puts Rowan and WOLF in the wrong places
problems.what_player_sees: The moment WOLF reaches the relay, the hint says 'The seal is open. Move to the safe point.' The red seal is still fully shut in that frame and only fades upward a beat later. The narration says 'WOLF holds the live contact by choice. Rowan keeps the breaker on; the red seal rises.' On screen Rowan stands at the relay, not the breaker, and WOLF has already let go and is walking away while the line still says he holds it. In R2 the line is 'WOLF reads the rising seal: "Open"' over a shut seal.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The text gets ahead of the effect and describes a scene that isn't on screen. You can't connect 'I did X, so Y happened' when Y is announced before it is shown and the positions are wrong.
problems.suggestion: Hold the 'seal is open' hint and objective until the rise animation finishes. Keep WOLF on the contact until the seal is fully up. Rewrite the line to match the positions, e.g. 'WOLF holds the live contact; the red seal grinds upward.' Or physically put Rowan back at the breaker.

problems.title: The mirror hint is stale after the copy and points the wrong way
problems.what_player_sees: Once the mirror index is copied, the card says REACH EXIT and the label says MIRROR COPIED, but the hint still reads 'E: examine the mirror port.' After Continue from the mirror save, the dialogue says 'Both traces are copied; head for the exit' with the same stale hint underneath.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The card and the hint now disagree, so a player may keep pressing E at a finished station or think the copy failed.
problems.suggestion: Refresh the hint when the mirror copy finishes and after a Continue restore, e.g. 'Mirror copied. Head for the exit.' Check every station for the same stale-hint pattern.

problems.title: The reason for the whole trip is hidden behind an optional display
problems.what_player_sees: The only line that explains the goal ('DIRECTOR / PURGE: Original program logs marked for deletion. WOLF: They want the source record gone. We need to preserve it.') appears only if you read the display marked 'READ DISPLAY (optional)'. Skip it (R1), and you get references to 'the original logs', 'the Director's purge is still running', 'purge order... target ID', 'the purge target existed before the deletion order' and 'A list doesn't tell me who's a threat' without ever learning what is being purged or what list he means.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: Every objective in Records (COPY PURGE ORDER, COPY MIRROR INDEX, FIRST COPY SECURED) depends on stakes the main path never states. The mirror finding is close to a tautology for a newcomer, and nobody shows 'the list' WOLF refers to.
problems.suggestion: Make the core line ('the Director is deleting the original program logs; we copy them first') required, either spoken on entering the corridor or shown when you first pass the display. Keep the display for optional extra detail. In Records, show the purge queue as a visible list of names or IDs, and give the mirror result one plain line of meaning (e.g. 'The target was flagged before any incident. The threat list is fake.').

problems.title: WOLF says he 'will not cross' the rubble, then crosses it
problems.what_player_sees: 'The seal goes. WOLF holds at the rubble and will not cross.' A few seconds later, if you ask, he walks into the lane under the tank to draw the sentry. In another run, after the same request, he refuses: 'No. I won't walk into its sights.' The game never says why he agrees in one run and refuses in another.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The narration states as a fixed fact something that one branch then breaks. Because the cause of his choice (your earlier honesty at the relay) is never surfaced, his behaviour looks random, not like a reaction to you.
problems.suggestion: Change the line to 'WOLF stops at the rubble and waits for your call.' When WOLF agrees or refuses, tie it to the earlier beat in one clause, e.g. 'You told me the truth at the relay. I'll draw it' versus 'You rushed me at the relay. I'm not walking into its sights.'

problems.title: The relay risk is set up and then never pays off
problems.what_player_sees: At the breaker the hint says 'E: ask WOLF about the relay risk', but nothing in the room shows a risk or a 'coolant fault'. WOLF then asks the player 'You know what "coolant fault" means. What happens if I touch the live relay?' Whoever takes the relay (WOLF in R1, Rowan in R2), no coolant ever vents and nothing bad happens.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The hint says you'll ask WOLF, but WOLF ends up asking you. The fault is never shown, and the risk the whole choice hangs on never happens. On a replay the player learns the warning was empty, and WOLF's refusal looks unreasonable because the human does the same job with no harm.
problems.suggestion: Put a visible COOLANT FAULT warning on the relay (blinking tag, frost, dripping). Change the hint to 'E: talk to WOLF about the relay.' Show a small payoff in each branch, e.g. a coolant puff that WOLF shrugs off, or that singes Rowan's sleeve on the bypass, so the warning was real.

problems.title: Rowan is never introduced, and the narration talks about him in the third person
problems.what_player_sees: The opening shows only the Director and WOLF in containment. In the corridor a red-jacket character appears with no introduction, first named in a dialogue line ('ROWAN: Then we get through maintenance...'). From then on the narration says 'Rowan keeps a local copy', 'Rowan takes the bypass', 'Rowan keeps the breaker on.'
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: A first-time player isn't told that they are Rowan, who Rowan is, or why Rowan is helping WOLF escape. Third-person narration about the player character also makes it unclear whether 'Rowan' is you.
problems.suggestion: Show Rowan in the opening (e.g. hiding as the engineer on shift who sees WOLF wake up), and add a one-line name card when control starts ('ROWAN / MAINTENANCE ENGINEER'). Keep player-action narration consistent, either 'You take the bypass' or a clearly established third person from the start.

problems.title: Narration lines are shown under the Director's name, and the dialogue format keeps changing
problems.what_player_sees: Under the DIRECTOR speaker tag, the second line is narration: 'He thinks WOLF is still in standby.' and 'WOLF turns from him and takes the only open route.' Other beats use inline 'DIRECTOR: ... / WOLF: ...' with no tag, and others mix 'Safe point saved. WOLF: ...' in one box.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: It reads as if the Director is narrating his own blind spot and WOLF's escape. Switching between a speaker tag, inline names and narration makes it hard to tell who is talking.
problems.suggestion: Split each line into its own box with the right speaker tag (narration untagged, in italics or another colour). Pick one format for multi-speaker beats and use it everywhere.

problems.title: WOLF walks back toward his cage on 'the only open route'
problems.what_player_sees: 'WOLF turns from him and takes the only open route.' WOLF walks left, back toward the containment cage he just left, and the scene cuts.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: No exit is shown, and the movement points back at the cage, which reads as WOLF going back in.
problems.suggestion: Show an open maintenance door or vent on the screen edge WOLF walks toward (ideally away from the cage), or have the gate open onto a passage behind the cage.

problems.title: Objectives and labels name things before they exist, or with confusing words
problems.what_player_sees: 'OPEN THE SEAL' and 'the red seal stays shut' appear while the seal is off-screen. 'DROP THE TANK' becomes the objective the moment the door blows, before any tank has been mentioned and while it is barely in view. 'ARM PANEL' (the crane arm) sits in a room where 'arm' is also the verb for the breakers ('Arm the breaker on the left', 'E: arm the overload breaker'). 'Arm the breaker on the left' is said while the player is standing left of it. The junction door is called a 'seal' (CHARGE THE SEAL) right after the corridor's red seal, which worked completely differently.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: Each one is small, but together they make a first-time player stop and wonder what a word refers to instead of acting on it.
problems.suggestion: Delay 'DROP THE TANK' until WOLF points out the tank (or briefly pan the camera to it). Rename ARM PANEL to CRANE PANEL or TANK RELEASE. Say 'the breaker by the entrance' instead of 'on the left'. Call the junction door a 'blast door', not a seal.

problems.title: The exit bolt runs on a 'spare overload' from a breaker labelled SPENT
problems.what_player_sees: The overload breaker is labelled BREAKER SPENT after the door blows. At the hatch: 'The spare overload runs into the exit bolt. The panel whines.'
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: No spare overload was ever mentioned, and the visible state says the power is used up. The player can't follow why the bolt works.
problems.suggestion: Either label the breaker 'BREAKER: RESERVE' after the blast, or give the bolt its own visible power source (a cell the tank fall knocks loose, or a panel WOLF powers). Change the line to match.

problems.title: Records exit: you 'secure a copy' at a door that stays shut
problems.what_player_sees: At the red EXIT door the hint is 'E: secure the first copy.' The result is 'FIRST COPY SECURED' while the door is still red and closed, and the next hint is 'E: follow the service line toward Archive.' Rowan then says 'Archive is next', but the next room is a Service Junction.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: Securing data at a door doesn't make sense, and the door's state (red, shut) doesn't change, so it looks like nothing happened.
problems.suggestion: Put a terminal or uplink by the exit labelled UPLINK and make that the 'secure' action. Have the exit visibly unlock (red to green) when the copy is secured. Say 'the service line to Archive' on the card so the junction reads as on the way.

problems.title: The save model isn't explained: the title says only safe points save, then knockdowns say 'last autosave'
problems.what_player_sees: The title says 'No checkpoint yet. Reach a SAFE POINT to save.' In the junction, which has no safe point, every knockdown ends with 'Back at the last autosave', and Continue resumes from several junction stages.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The player is told saving only happens at safe points and then finds hidden autosaves. That's harmless but confusing, and it leaves the player unsure what Continue will restore.
problems.suggestion: Show a small 'Checkpoint' toast when an autosave happens, and change the title note to 'Progress saves at safe points and checkpoints.'

problems.title: The slice ending drops you to the title with no end card, and Continue leads to a dead end
problems.what_player_sees: After 'SERVICE LINE CLEARED... Then that's where we go.' and E CONTINUE, the game cuts straight to the title screen. Continue then puts you back in the junction with 'The hatch is open. The line beyond it is not built yet.'
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: With no 'end of chapter / demo' card, the cut to the title can look like a crash or a reset. Continuing into a room that only says 'not built yet' feels like a bug, not an ending.
problems.suggestion: Add an 'END OF SLICE: thanks for playing' card with a recap of the player's choices before the title. Change the Continue note on the title to 'Slice complete' (or offer a replay) instead of loading into the dead end.

problems.title: The Settings tab highlight stays on DISPLAY while Audio and Controls are shown
problems.what_player_sees: The Audio sliders and the Controls binding table are both shown with the DISPLAY tab still highlighted.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The selected tab doesn't match the content, so you can't tell which tab you're on. (This may be because the driver switched tabs without moving focus. Check it by hand with the mouse and the controller.)
problems.suggestion: Tie the tab highlight to the selected tab, not to focus, and move focus to the selected tab when it changes.

problems.title: Small wording and framing inconsistencies
problems.what_player_sees: 'Hold USE to crank it' in dialogue, 'HOLD E' in the hint and 'Interact / continue' in Controls. 'CORRIDOR CLEARED' though nothing was cleared. WOLF clipped at the left screen edge after Continue from junction save A or a knockdown restore. 'THE DEN / LOCAL CONFIGURATION' header in Settings, never explained. The tutorial box and the hint bar repeat the same 'read display' prompt.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: Three names for one button, an objective that names nothing, and a companion half off-screen each add a little friction for a newcomer.
problems.suggestion: Use one action name everywhere (show the bound key, e.g. 'Hold E'). Change CORRIDOR CLEARED to SEAL OPEN or SAFE POINT REACHED. Restore WOLF fully on screen. Drop the tutorial box's copy of the hint text.

what_works: World labels change state with every action (BREAKER to BREAKER LIVE to BREAKER SPENT, VALVE 0/3 to SEAL CHARGED, SEALED DOOR to DOOR DOWN, ARM PANEL to ARM REWINDING to TANK DOWN, EXIT BOLTED to EXIT OPEN, PURGE COPIED, MIRROR COPIED). Cause and effect can be read from the labels alone (R1-043, R1-050, R2-051, R1-067).

The objective card moves step by step and nearly always matches the next interaction (CHECK THE BREAKER, ARM THE BREAKER, OPEN THE SEAL, REACH SAFE POINT; CLEAR THE LINE, CHARGE THE SEAL, CLEAR THE DOOR, DROP THE TANK, POP THE EXIT BOLT).

The valve crank gives clear progress feedback in three places at once: the hint ('HOLD E: crank the valve, 1 of 3 turns'), the dialogue ('The valve gives. 2 of 3 turns.') and the three-bar meter filling to green (R1-047 to R1-049).

Knockdown messages say what killed you and how to avoid it ('Stand clear of the grate when the gauge peaks', 'Cross when it faces away, or get back over the rubble'), then restore quickly to the start of the current puzzle (R3-069/070, R3-107/108).

The missed-drop loop is readable as a sequence: coolant cloud, sentry chases, 'Stay back over the rubble until it gives up', 'It lost you', 'The winch has the tank back on the clamp. The ARM PANEL is ready again.' (R2-051 to R2-055).

WOLF reads as his own character: he agrees when told the truth and refuses when rushed. The safe point quotes your exact words back to you ('You said "Go now. We can talk after." I refused. You found another way.'), which makes the choice feel heard (R1-025, R2-017, R4-017).
Every WOLF-dependent step has an engineer-only fallback that works and is spelled out: manual bypass, manual mirror port, timing the drop yourself from the panel (R2-013/014, R2-025, R2-047).
WOLF's 'I'll hold at the rubble. It crosses the floor mark on every pass; the tank takes a moment to fall.' is a good, fair lead-in for the timing puzzle (R2-047).
Continue from every save restores the right objective, with a one-line 'restored' summary of where you are (R3-020, R3-025, R3-032, R3-049, R3-099, R3-120, R3-127).
The pause menu is honest about what Return to Title keeps and loses, and the line gauge stays frozen while paused (R3-060 to R3-065). The Audio tab honestly says there is no music or voice yet.
The art reads well at 1280x720: big station labels, a clear floor-mark bracket for the tank, and a visible drawn frame for the panel alcove. The alcove rule just needs to match that frame.

problems.title: The junction's 'sealed door' sits in the back wall, opens onto more wall, and never blocked the lane
problems.what_player_sees: The SEALED DOOR faces the camera in the back wall. The ARM PANEL, the hanging tank and the floor mark are already on screen to its right, on the same floor the engineer stands on (R1-038, R1-049). When the door blows, the ragged hole shows more pipes and wall behind it (R1-050, R1-053). The engineer never walks through it. They walk right along the floor past the frame to the panel (R1-054).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: A door in the back wall cannot stop someone walking sideways. The panel and the tank look reachable before the door is blown, so the whole breaker, valve and blast sequence seems to unlock nothing. Through the hole the door leads to a wall, which is the 'door opens onto a wall' defect.
problems.suggestion: Make the sealed door a bulkhead that crosses the walking lane, side-on like a wall section, with the panel, tank and sentry hidden or dark behind it until it blows. Or keep the back-wall door and show the lane continuing through it into a second plane or room. Either way, the area past the door should not be visible and reachable-looking beforehand.

problems.title: The corridor seal stands alone on open floor and vanishes instead of rising
problems.what_player_sees: The red seal is a free-standing pillar between the relay and the safe point. No wall, frame or ceiling is attached to it (R1-019, R1-021). The text says 'the red seal rises'. The pillar drops slightly and then disappears completely, leaving bare floor and wall (R1-022, R1-023).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: A door with no wall around it blocks nothing, because you could walk around it. Its disappearance does not match 'rises'. Nothing shows where it went.
problems.suggestion: Set the seal into a full-height bulkhead or frame across the corridor, and animate it sliding up into a header that stays visible as an open doorway.

problems.title: No one holds the contact or keeps the breaker on, yet the seal stays open
problems.what_player_sees: The line reads 'WOLF holds the live contact by choice. Rowan keeps the breaker on; the red seal rises.' Rowan is standing at the relay, about 250 px from the breaker (R1-021). Within a second WOLF lets go and walks away (R1-023). Both then stand at the safe point while the seal stays open (R1-024, R1-025).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The text describes two people holding things to keep the door open. On screen, neither is holding anything, and the door stays open anyway. The breaker is a latching lever that needs no one at it.
problems.suggestion: Rewrite as a one-shot action: 'WOLF takes the surge through the live contact; the seal latches open.' Or, if holding matters, keep WOLF on the contact until the engineer is through and have the seal close behind them.

problems.title: The 'manual bypass' is the same relay box, which makes WOLF's risk pointless
problems.what_player_sees: After WOLF refuses, or while he is still walking to the contact, Rowan presses E on the same COOLANT RELAY box. An orange spark appears and the seal opens (R2-013, R2-014, R4-013, R4-014). No separate bypass object or label exists.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The human touches the box WOLF called too dangerous and nothing happens to them. There is no visible bypass, and nothing shows a cost or difference. If a free, safe bypass exists, an engineer would never ask WOLF to take a live coolant contact. That empties the disclose/press choice of meaning in the world.
problems.suggestion: Add a separate, labelled MANUAL BYPASS panel a few steps away with a visible cost: a hold-to-crank, a timer, a coolant puff the engineer must step back from, or a longer route. Then WOLF taking the contact is the fast option, and the bypass is the slower, engineer-only fallback.

problems.title: After WOLF refuses at the breaker, the relay still offers to ask him again
problems.what_player_sees: WOLF: 'No. I won't take that risk blind. Use the bypass.' (R2-009). At the relay the hint still reads 'E: ask WOLF to take the live relay.' (R2-012). WOLF refuses a second time and says 'Press E again for the manual bypass.' (R2-013).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The world has already said no. The game makes the player ask again and then breaks the fiction with a key prompt in WOLF's own line.
problems.suggestion: After a refusal, change the relay hint straight to 'E: take the manual bypass.' Remove the control instruction from WOLF's dialogue.

problems.title: WOLF promises to keep clear of the tank, then stands under it when it drops
problems.what_player_sees: WOLF: 'I'll draw it onto the mark and keep clear of the tank.' He then stands inside the yellow floor brackets, directly under the hanging tank, nose to nose with the sentry (R1-058). The drop prompt appears with him still there (R1-060), and the tank falls (R1-061, R1-062).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The engineer is told to drop a tank onto a spot their companion is standing on. WOLF's line and his position contradict each other. Doing this would kill him.
problems.suggestion: Have WOLF bait from just outside the mark, for example one body-length to the right, so the sentry stops on the mark facing him. Or show him leaping clear when the clamp releases.

problems.title: A hit and a miss look backwards
problems.what_player_sees: R2: the tank lands in the coolant cloud right over the sentry's position, but it counts as a miss and the sentry gives chase (R2-051, R2-052). R4: the clamp lets go while the sentry is about 100 px right of the floor mark, beside the bolt box (R4-049). That drop counts as a hit: 'comes down square and crushes the sentry flat' (R4-051).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The visible result should decide the outcome. Here a drop that looks on target misses, and a drop that looks clearly off target hits. The player cannot learn the timing from what they see.
problems.suggestion: Resolve hit or miss from whether the sentry's body overlaps the tank's footprint at impact, and draw the result that way: the sentry clearly beside the tank on a miss, clearly under it on a hit. Keep the floor-mark brackets the same width as the hit zone.

problems.title: 'The ARM PANEL alcove hides you' while the engineer stands at the rubble and the sentry is parked in the alcove
problems.what_player_sees: The line says 'It lost you and goes back to its patrol. The ARM PANEL alcove hides you from it.' Rowan is standing in the blown doorway on the rubble, and the sentry sits directly in front of the arm panel inside the alcove outline (R2-054). In R3 the sentry runs Rowan down right in front of the panel, inside the same alcove (R3-107).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The alcove is a flat outlined rectangle in the same plane as the lane. It does not look like cover, the sentry drives into it, and the line names a hiding place the engineer is not in.
problems.suggestion: Draw the alcove as a real recess, set back with side walls and darker, and stop the sentry's patrol at its edge. Make the lose-it line match where the engineer actually is ('The rubble breaks its line of sight').

problems.title: Open exits become flat placeholder boxes
problems.what_player_sees: The Records EXIT is the same red seal sprite. After 'secure the first copy' it turns into a flat navy rectangle with a grey outline (R1-036, R1-037). The junction hatch shows 'The hatch slides open' while its sprite is still closed (R1-066). It then becomes a flat teal box (R1-067, R1-070).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: An opened door should show a passage. These doors lead to a featureless panel, and in R1-066 the text says open while the art says shut.
problems.suggestion: Give each exit an open-state sprite: the door slid up or aside, with a lit corridor or darkness behind it. Switch the art on the same frame the text says it opens.

problems.title: The valve that blows the door sits in the blast zone, and the escape route crosses the relief vent
problems.what_player_sees: The only valve is bolted against the sealed door (R1-046). Once charged, the hint says 'Get left of the vent, away from the door.' (R1-049). To obey, the engineer has to run back over the relief-vent grate, which they were told to stay off. Standing at the valve gets 'The door blew with you in front of it.' (R3-081).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: No engineer would put the firing control for a breaching charge next to the charge. The safe zone sits behind another hazard. The hint also points past the vent when the real safe line is just right of it.
problems.suggestion: Either move the valve to the far side of the vent, so the engineer cranks from cover and the door blows at a distance, or say plainly in the world why it is close: a short fuse, plus a painted blast line on the floor to get behind. Point the hint at that line, not 'left of the vent'.

problems.title: Knockdown frames contradict their own text and WOLF ignores the hazards he warns about
problems.what_player_sees: In the blast knockdown the door is drawn intact with the SEALED DOOR label, while the text says it blew (R3-081). WOLF stands inside the vent steam column and in front of the door during the charge and both knockdowns, unharmed (R1-046, R1-049, R3-069, R3-081). Yet he warns 'Don't stand in front of it when it goes.'
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The hazard the player was hit by is not shown going off. Their companion stands in the same spot untouched, so the danger reads as arbitrary.
problems.suggestion: Show the door blowing in the blast knockdown frame before the reset. Have WOLF step clear of the vent and the door once the line is live, for example to the breaker side.

problems.title: WOLF 'will not cross' the rubble, then crosses it
problems.what_player_sees: The line says 'WOLF holds at the rubble and will not cross'. WOLF actually stands inside the blown door frame on the rubble (R1-053). After the bait choice he walks well past the rubble into the lane under the tank (R1-058).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The stated boundary is broken within seconds. The rubble lies in the doorway, which the lane does not run through, so it is not a line across the path.
problems.suggestion: Change the line to 'WOLF holds at the rubble' with no 'will not cross', or make the bait choice an explicit exception ('I'll cross if you need me to'). Put the rubble on the lane floor so it reads as a line.

problems.title: The sentry appears in a lit area that was visibly empty
problems.what_player_sees: Before the blast, the floor past the door, under the tank and up to the bolt box, is lit and empty (R1-038, R1-049). After the blast the line says 'something answers from the dark past the door' and a sentry is suddenly patrolling there (R1-053).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: Nothing was dark and nothing was 'past the door'. The sentry seems to appear from thin air in a space the player could see.
problems.suggestion: Keep that area unlit or out of view until the door blows, or show the sentry dormant in a recess and powering up with its eyes lighting on the blast.

problems.title: A ruptured tank is winched back up and reused, and the 'released' tank is still on a cable
problems.what_player_sees: On a miss the tank 'hits the floor and vents coolant' (R2-051). Then 'The winch has the tank back on the clamp' and it drops again intact (R2-055). In every landed frame the tank is still linked to the arm by a coiled cable after 'The clamp lets go' (R1-063, R1-064). The TANK DOWN label floats over the arm panel, not the tank.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: A tank that just burst should not be reusable. A dropped tank should not stay tethered. The status label sits on the wrong object.
problems.suggestion: On a miss, have the tank bounce or dent without venting and get winched back. Or vent and swap in a second tank from a rack. Remove the cable once the clamp releases, or call it a 'winch cable' that pays out. Put TANK DOWN or ARM status on the arm or tank.

problems.title: The ARM PANEL is the same lever box as the breakers
problems.what_player_sees: The ARM PANEL uses the identical lever-box sprite as the corridor BREAKER and the junction OVERLOAD BREAKER (R1-010, R1-038). No cable, conduit or schematic line joins it to the overhead arm and tank, unlike the drawn line from the breaker to the vent, valve and door.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: Players learn that this sprite means 'breaker'. Nothing shows that this one releases a clamp on a tank a screen-width away.
problems.suggestion: Give the arm panel its own look, such as a release lever with a red guard or a clamp icon, and run the same style of schematic line from it up to the arm.

problems.title: The 'spare overload' for the exit bolt comes from nowhere
problems.what_player_sees: 'The spare overload runs into the exit bolt.' (R1-065). The overload breaker is labelled BREAKER SPENT and the line was used up in the blast. The bolt box has cables to the hatch, but no line to any power source.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The game made a point of spending the overload on the door. A second, unseen one undercuts the cause and effect it just taught.
problems.suggestion: Extend the schematic line to the bolt box, for example 'the arm panel's feed reroutes to the bolt once the tank is down', or give the bolt its own visible power cell.

problems.title: The mirror hint goes stale after the copy
problems.what_player_sees: The station label reads MIRROR COPIED and the objective reads REACH EXIT, but the hint still says 'E: examine the mirror port.' (R1-033). The same happens after Continue with both traces copied (R3-041, R3-042).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The prompt sends the player back to a finished station.
problems.suggestion: Once mirror_trace is set, change the mirror hint to 'Mirror copied. Head for the exit.'

problems.title: You secure the copy at a door
problems.what_player_sees: 'E: secure the first copy' fires at the EXIT door (R1-035, R1-036). That door is the red sealed-door sprite and stays red while it is used.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: Securing a data copy is a terminal action, not a door action. The red lock colour says the exit is shut.
problems.suggestion: Put a small upload or vault terminal beside the exit for 'secure the first copy', and have the exit turn green or open once it is done.

problems.title: Corridor to Records has no doorway
problems.what_player_sees: 'E: enter records access' fires at the safe point. The corridor's right end is a solid pipe wall (R1-025). Records opens with the engineer in front of pipes and a tank on the left, with no entry door (R1-026).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The player moves between rooms through a wall. Every other transition (the junction's vault door at the left, the hatch at the right) shows a door.
problems.suggestion: Add a 'RECORDS' door past the safe point in the corridor and a matching door at the left of Records.

problems.title: The opening exits left, back past the cage, and Rowan appears from nowhere
problems.what_player_sees: 'WOLF turns from him and takes the only open route.' WOLF walks left, back toward and past his own cage, while the open room extends to the right (R1-008, R1-009). The corridor then starts with WOLF at the left edge and Rowan already next to him, talking (R1-010). Rowan was never in the containment room.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: Leaving to the left and entering the next room from the left flips direction. 'The only open route' points back toward the cage. The engineer, the only playable character, appears with no entrance or introduction.
problems.suggestion: Have WOLF exit right, past the Director, through a visible maintenance door. Open the corridor with Rowan arriving or being found there, with one line establishing who Rowan is.

problems.title: 'The seal is open' shows while the seal is still closed
problems.what_player_sees: The hint 'The seal is open. Move to the safe point.' appears while the red seal is still fully drawn and lit (R1-021, R2-014, R4-014).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: Text and art disagree on the frame where it matters most.
problems.suggestion: Show 'The seal is opening' during the animation and switch to 'is open' when the art finishes.

problems.title: The engineer is drawn behind or inside machines
problems.what_player_sees: Rowan is hidden inside the coolant relay behind the spark effect (R1-021, R1-022). Only Rowan's head shows behind the purge queue (R1-026). Rowan stands inside the mirror port (R1-032, R1-033).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: Layering puts the player character inside solid equipment, so it is unclear where they are standing.
problems.suggestion: Draw the characters in front of interactables, or stop the engineer at a use spot beside each machine rather than at its centre.

problems.title: After Continue or a restore, WOLF is clipped into the left wall
problems.what_player_sees: After Continue from junction save A, and after knockdown restores, WOLF starts half off-screen, overlapping the vault door and the left wall (R3-057, R3-082).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The companion appears partly inside a wall.
problems.suggestion: Restore WOLF to the same visible spot as a fresh entry, beside the engineer and inside the room bounds.

problems.title: Small continuity slips: the cage bars vanish, a repeated prop, and WOLF asking about a 'live' relay too early
problems.what_player_sees: 'The gate slides aside', but the cage bars simply disappear (R1-004 to R1-006). The Records PURGE QUEUE is the exact sprite of the corridor's Director purge display (R1-010, R1-026). At the breaker, before it is armed, WOLF asks 'What happens if I touch the live relay?' (R1-015).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: These are small breaks: an animation the text describes but the art does not show, a reused machine that suggests the same station twice, and the relay called live before it is powered.
problems.suggestion: Slide the gate sprite aside. Tint or redress the Records purge queue. Change WOLF's line to 'once the relay goes live'.

what_works: The junction's drawn schematic line from the overload breaker down to the relief vent, the valve and the sealed door clearly shows what feeds what. On a vent trip the whole line turns red and the label becomes BREAKER TRIPPED (R1-038, R3-069).

Object labels update with state, so progress can be read at a glance: BREAKER LIVE / SPENT, VALVE 0/3 then SEAL CHARGED / SPENT, DOOR DOWN, ARM REWINDING, TANK DOWN, EXIT BOLTED / OPEN, PURGE COPIED, MIRROR COPIED (R1-043, R1-050, R2-051, R1-066).
The three-light turn counter beside the valve, plus its pressure gauge, give physical feedback for the stiff hold-to-crank wheel (R1-047, R1-049).
The floor-mark brackets sit directly under the hanging tank, so 'it lands on the floor mark' matches the layout (R1-054, R1-060).
The corridor order (breaker, then relay lights up blue, then seal) is cause-and-effect the player can see: the relay's indicator lights when the breaker catches (R1-015 to R1-017).
The junction starts in front of a large wheel-vault door at the left and ends at a matching vault hatch at the right, which gives the room believable entry and exit points (R1-038, R1-064).
The blown door art (twisted frame, hazard tape, rubble) reads clearly as a breach (R1-053).
Records shows a clear, ordered station layout (purge queue, mirror port, exit) with a hint that names that order (R1-026).

Knockdowns name the specific cause and the fix ('The relief vent let go under you. Stand clear of the grate when the gauge peaks.'), and restores put the engineer back at a sensible autosave with the right objective (R3-069, R3-070, R3-107, R3-108).
The Continue restore lines state exactly what is already done ('Both traces are copied; head for the exit', 'The door is down; the sentry patrols the lane past the rubble') (R3-041, R3-099).
The safe point quotes the player's own relay choice back to them, which ties the save to what they did (R1-025, R2-017).
Pausing and the Settings tabs freeze the building line; the gauge holds at 0.11 throughout (R3-060 to R3-065).

problems.title: The engineer is never introduced: no reason they are here, who they are, or why they help WOLF
problems.what_player_sees: The opening (R1-002 to R1-009) shows only the Director and the caged WOLF. The engineer never appears. The first gameplay frame (R1-010) has the engineer already standing beside WOLF in the corridor, and the name 'ROWAN:' appears for the first time on a dialogue line. WOLF then tells Rowan what the player just watched ('I heard the Director's plan for me. I woke myself...'), and Rowan agrees on the spot to get through maintenance.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The title art (R1-001) shows the engineer and WOLF together, but the game never shows how they met, what the engineer's job is, or why a person who just watched a military robot break out would trust it straight away. WOLF explaining his own awakening to someone who seemingly was not there, and that person signing on in one line, reads as two scenes stitched together. The player does not know who they are playing.
problems.suggestion: Put the engineer in the containment room, or add a short beat as WOLF reaches maintenance: the engineer is working on WOLF's equipment, sees him, and is given a reason to trust him (WOLF warns them, or the engineer recognises his own work on the body). Add one line of identity, such as 'ROWAN (systems engineer)', before Rowan first speaks. Then WOLF's corridor line can be addressed to someone who did not hear the Director.

problems.title: The evidence thread does not add up: original logs, a purge order, a 'list', 'the source' and Archive are never connected
problems.what_player_sees: Rowan's first line refers to 'the original logs' (R1-010) before anything has mentioned logs. The only explanation is the optional purge display (R3-005: 'Original program logs marked for deletion'), which R1, R2 and R4 never read. In Records the player copies 'a time and target ID' while 'the original logs are still missing' (R1-028). WOLF's readout then shows 'The purge target existed before the deletion order' (R1-033), the card reads FIRST COPY SECURED, and WOLF says 'A list doesn't tell me who's a threat. I want the source.' Rowan replies 'Then Archive is next' (R1-036).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The goal stated at the start (save the original logs) is never met or let go; the game swaps in 'copy the purge order' without saying why that helps. 'Target ID' could mean a deleted record or a person the Director wants WOLF to hunt, and the game never says which. 'Existed before the deletion order' is true of anything that gets deleted, so it does not read as a discovery. No list is ever shown, so 'a list' points at nothing. Archive is named for the first time as the next destination. The player cannot say what they secured or why it matters to the Director's plan to make WOLF hunt people.
problems.suggestion: Make the purge setup required: have WOLF react to the display on the way past, or move its line into the opening. Then state the chain in plain words: the purge deletes the original logs; the purge order shows who ordered it and what it targets; the mirror timestamp proves the record existed before the Director ordered it erased, so it is a cover-up and not cleanup. If the target is a person, say so. Replace 'A list' with what was actually copied, and name Archive earlier as the place the originals are kept.

problems.title: After WOLF refuses the relay, the game still offers 'ask WOLF to take the live relay', and he has to refuse again while telling the player to 'Press E'
problems.what_player_sees: WOLF says 'No. I won't take that risk blind. Use the bypass.' (R2-009). At the relay the hint still reads 'E: ask WOLF to take the live relay.' (R2-012). Pressing it makes WOLF say 'I said no. I won't take the live contact. Press E again for the manual bypass.' (R2-013). The same happens in R3-012/013. In the honest route WOLF has already said 'I'll take the relay. Arm the breaker.' (R1-016), but the hint still asks the player to ask him (R1-019).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The game pushes the player to repeat a request WOLF has already refused, which undercuts his refusal and makes the engineer look like they ignored him. In the cooperative route it asks for something he has already agreed to. A control prompt ('Press E again') spoken in WOLF's own voice breaks character.
problems.suggestion: After a refusal, make the relay hint 'E: take the manual bypass.' only. After agreement, have WOLF walk to the contact when the breaker catches, with no second ask. Keep control prompts in the hint bar and out of WOLF's dialogue.

problems.title: The manual bypass is free and always available, so letting WOLF take the live relay is pointless
problems.what_player_sees: As soon as WOLF heads for the contact, the hint offers 'E: take the manual bypass instead.' (R1-020, R4-013). Taking it opens the seal at once with no cost: 'Rowan takes the bypass. WOLF reads the rising seal: "Open. I'm with you."' (R2-014, R4-014). The coolant vent that WOLF asked about never happens on any route. In R4 the engineer overrides WOLF after he has volunteered, and WOLF answers only 'You took the bypass. I stayed with you.' (R4-017).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The relay choice is framed as a real risk, but there is a safe option with no downside, so asking WOLF to touch a live contact makes the engineer look careless and makes WOLF's courage mean nothing. When WOLF is overridden after offering, his reply does not register what happened.
problems.suggestion: Give the bypass a visible cost: it is slower, it sets off the lockdown alarm, or the engineer takes a brief coolant hit. Or show that WOLF's frame can survive the vent where a person cannot, so his offer makes sense. Give R4 its own line, for example 'I offered. You didn't let me. ...noted.'

problems.title: 'WOLF holds at the rubble and will not cross', and then he crosses to bait the sentry
problems.what_player_sees: When the door blows, the narration says 'WOLF holds at the rubble and will not cross' (R1-050). If the player picks 'Draw it under the arm if you can stay clear', WOLF walks past the rubble into the lane and stands beside the sentry under the tank (R1-057, R1-058).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The narration states a firm boundary, and the next choice has him break it without comment. It is unclear whether his refusal in R3 ('No. I won't walk into its sights', R3-103) comes from that boundary or from how he was treated.
problems.suggestion: Change the narration to 'WOLF stops at the rubble and waits' (a pause, not a refusal), so that crossing later is his decision in response to the engineer's request.

problems.title: After a missed drop, the text says the alcove hides the engineer while the sentry sits in the alcove; the miss also looks like a hit
problems.what_player_sees: The tank lands with a coolant cloud right next to the sentry, yet the text reports a miss: 'The sentry turns on the panel; get back over the rubble.' (R2-051, R2-052). A few seconds later: 'It lost you and goes back to its patrol. The ARM PANEL alcove hides you from it.' In that frame the sentry is parked in the ARM PANEL alcove, and the engineer is at the rubble (R2-054).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The player is told to flee over the rubble, then told the alcove is what hid them, while the shot shows the sentry inside the alcove. 'Turns on the panel' can also be read as 'switches the panel on'. A tank that lands in a cloud touching the sentry does not look like a miss.
problems.suggestion: Write the lose line from where the engineer actually is: 'It lost you behind the rubble and goes back to its patrol.' Change 'turns on the panel' to 'swings toward the panel'. Make misses clearly wide, or describe the near-miss: 'It clips the sentry's track and it lurches clear.'

problems.title: 'Get left of the vent' sends the player through the hazard they were just told to avoid
problems.what_player_sees: When the line peaks, the relief vent is erupting (a visible steam column), and both the dialogue and the hint say 'Get left of the vent before the fuse ends' / 'Get left of the vent, away from the door.' (R1-049, R3-080). The engineer is at the valve, right of the vent. Standing still gives 'The door blew with you in front of it.' (R3-081). The earlier vent knockdown says 'Stand clear of the grate when the gauge peaks.' (R3-069).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The only way to get left of the vent is to walk through it while it is going off. The two pieces of advice contradict each other, and the hint names the wrong landmark for the safe area.
problems.suggestion: Name a landmark that matches the real blast area ('Back off from the door, past the valve'), or make sure the vent is quiet when the fuse is lit and say so ('The vent has spent itself; get behind it').

problems.title: WOLF's refusal to bait the sentry gives no hint that it comes from the earlier relay treatment
problems.what_player_sees: In R1 (risk disclosed), WOLF agrees to draw the sentry. In R3 (pressed at the relay), the same polite, caveated request gets 'No. I won't walk into its sights...' (R3-103). Nothing mentions the relay. In between, WOLF willingly gave his mirror readout (R3-038).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The game remembers the relay moment, which is good, but the refusal looks arbitrary because the request itself already included 'if you can stay clear', the same kind of honesty that earned a yes before. Cooperating at the mirror and then refusing here, with no stated reason, makes his trust look random.
problems.suggestion: Add one clause linking it back: 'Last time you sent me in blind. Not this time. You can time it from the panel.' Then the remembered choice is visible and fair.

problems.title: The mirror hint and the 'by his own choice' wording do not match what just happened
problems.what_player_sees: The player picks 'USE WOLF'S READOUT', and the narration says 'WOLF brings the mirror timestamp by his own choice.' The hint still reads 'E: examine the mirror port.' while the card says REACH EXIT and the station is labelled MIRROR COPIED (R1-033, R2-025, R4-025). It is the same after Continue: 'Both traces are copied; head for the exit.' with the hint still on the mirror port (R3-041).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The player chose to use WOLF's readout, so 'by his own choice' credits WOLF for the player's decision. The leftover hint points the player back at a finished task.
problems.suggestion: Say 'WOLF hands over the timestamp he found.' His independent choice was going to check the mirror, and the text can say that when he walks there. Change the hint to the exit once the mirror is copied.

problems.title: Narration is shown under the DIRECTOR speaker label
problems.what_player_sees: The box labelled DIRECTOR contains 'I decide who counts as a threat. WOLF handles the rest.' followed by 'He thinks WOLF is still in standby.' (R1-002). Later, under DIRECTOR: 'Lock down maintenance...' followed by 'WOLF turns from him and takes the only open route.' (R1-008, R1-009).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The Director appears to describe himself in the third person ('He thinks...') and to narrate WOLF walking away from him. That muddles the first impression of the antagonist.
problems.suggestion: Split each into two boxes: the Director's spoken line, then unlabelled narration.

problems.title: WOLF quotes a 'coolant fault' the player has never seen
problems.what_player_sees: At the breaker WOLF asks: 'You know what 'coolant fault' means. What happens if I touch the live relay?' (R1-015). Nothing before this shows or mentions a coolant fault (R1-010 to R1-014).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The quote marks suggest the phrase was shown somewhere, so the player feels they missed something. It is also why the engineer is the one who knows the risk, which matters to the honesty choice.
problems.suggestion: Show 'COOLANT FAULT' on the relay's panel or label as the player approaches, or have the engineer read it out. Then WOLF's question shows he trusts the engineer's expertise.

problems.title: Continue from the first junction save skips WOLF's blast warning
problems.what_player_sees: A fresh entry gives 'WOLF runs ahead to read the pressure...' and 'It's live. Don't stand in front of it when it goes.' (R1-038, R1-039). Continue from junction save A starts with WOLF behind the engineer at the far left and only 'Service junction restored. Arm the breaker...' (R3-056, R3-057).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: A player who continues here never hears the one line that warns about the door blast, so the blast knockdown feels unfair. WOLF's independent scouting moment is also lost.
problems.suggestion: Replay WOLF's scouting walk and warning on restore, or add the warning to the restore line ('...WOLF: Remember, don't stand in front of it.').

problems.title: The relay result text and visuals disagree
problems.what_player_sees: 'WOLF holds the live contact by choice. Rowan keeps the breaker on; the red seal rises.' In the frame the engineer is standing at the coolant relay, not the breaker, WOLF is behind them, and the red seal is still shown shut while the hint says 'The seal is open.' (R1-021, R1-022). R2-014 also shows the seal closed under 'The seal is open'.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The player cannot see WOLF doing the risky thing he chose, and the engineer is not where the text says. The payoff of the cooperation choice is not visible.
problems.suggestion: Have WOLF step up to the relay with a visible arc or contact pose while the engineer stays back. Only show 'The seal is open' after the seal animation finishes.

problems.title: 'We can talk after' is never followed up
problems.what_player_sees: Option 2 at the relay is 'Go now. We can talk after.' (R1-015). WOLF quotes it at the safe point (R2-017), but no later talk ever happens in Records or the junction.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The engineer's promise is the phrase the game remembers, yet there is no 'after'. A short follow-up would make WOLF's memory feel meaningful.
problems.suggestion: At the Records entrance on the press route, let WOLF call it in: 'You said we'd talk after. This is after.'

problems.title: Small wording issues in WOLF's Records entry line and the end-of-slice message
problems.what_player_sees: 'I chose the relay. I'm checking this path too.' (R1-026), where 'this path too' is vague. After Continue on a cleared save: 'The service line runs on past the hatch. That part is not built yet.' (R1-072, R3-129).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: 'Checking this path too' does not say what is being checked. 'Not built yet' is a developer note shown in the game's voice.
problems.suggestion: 'I chose the relay. I'll take the mirror here too.' For the end, use an in-world placeholder ('The hatch to Archive is open. END OF CURRENT BUILD') on a separate card, not in dialogue.

what_works: The self-awakening is staged clearly and in order: the Director thinks WOLF is in standby, 'Nobody gives an activation command. WOLF wakes himself', the latch breaks from the inside, and 'I heard you. I won't do it.' WOLF's independence and his refusal of the Director's plan are clear (R1-002 to R1-008).
The Director's aim is simple and chilling: 'I decide who counts as a threat. WOLF handles the rest.' WOLF restates it for the player: 'He wants me to hunt people he calls threats' (R1-002, R1-010).
The relay choice has a consistent result: telling WOLF the risk earns 'Thank you for telling me. I'll take the relay', and pressing him earns 'I won't take that risk blind' (R1-016, R2-009).

The safe point quotes the engineer's exact words and the actual outcome on every route, including the R4 override ('You said "The relay may vent coolant. Your call." You took the bypass.'), so the memory feels real (R1-025, R2-017, R4-017).

The Records entry line changes with the relay outcome ('I chose the relay' / 'I refused the live relay; I'm still here' / 'You used the manual bypass'), and WOLF's refusal never costs his later help at the mirror (R1-026, R2-018, R4-018).

Every WOLF-dependent step has a working engineer-only fallback (manual bypass, manual port, timed drop), and the narration credits the engineer by name ('Rowan copies the timestamp...') (R2-014, R2-025, R2-060).
WOLF visibly acts on his own: he walks to the mirror and runs ahead to read the junction door pressure before the player asks (R1-029, R1-038, R1-039).

The junction's cause and effect reads well: blowing the door makes noise, 'something answers from the dark', and the sentry is clearly a small tracked machine. Crushing it does not clash with WOLF refusing to hunt people (R1-050, R1-063).

Even when WOLF refuses to bait, he gives the engineer a usable tip ('It crosses the floor mark on every pass; you can time the drop from the panel'), and after a knockdown the choice can be made again (R3-103, R3-111).

Restore and Continue messages match the save state and say what to do next (R3-020, R3-025, R3-032, R3-049, R3-099, R3-120). Knockdown messages explain the cause and how to avoid it (R3-069, R3-081, R3-107).

problems.title: The tank drop gives opposite results for setups that look the same, so the main puzzle can't be learned
problems.what_player_sees: R2-050: the player drops while the sentry is far right by the generator, outside the floor mark. R2-051/052: the tank lands and visibly sits on top of the sentry in the coolant cloud, yet the game says 'The tank hits the floor and vents coolant. The sentry turns on the panel', which is a miss. R4-049/050: the player drops with the sentry in almost the same place (far right, outside the mark, still driving toward WOLF). This time R4-051 says 'The tank comes down square and crushes the sentry flat', and the sentry is suddenly crushed on the mark. R2-059: a drop with the sentry just right of the mark is also a hit. In R4 the drop came before 'it stops', even though WOLF said 'Drop it when it stops' (R1-055/R4-047).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: A tank that lands on the sentry is called a miss, while a tank dropped when the sentry is outside the mark is a hit. That only happens because WOLF is baiting. The floor mark, the falling tank and WOLF's instruction all point to a rule the game doesn't follow. Players will read the miss as a bug and the R4 hit as luck.
problems.suggestion: Use one visible rule: a hit means the sentry's body is inside the floor mark when the tank lands. Never draw the landed tank overlapping a sentry that survived, and push a missed sentry visibly clear of the tank. Don't snap a sentry outside the mark onto it. If WOLF is baiting, only light the ARM PANEL prompt (or turn it green) once the sentry has stopped on the mark, which matches 'Drop it when it stops'.

problems.title: Autosaves are never announced, but failures and Continue rely on them
problems.what_player_sees: The title says 'No checkpoint yet. Reach a SAFE POINT to save.' (R1-001). Only the corridor safe point ever says 'Safe point saved.' (R1-025). Entering Records, copying traces, finishing Records and each junction stage show no save message. Later, Continue drops the player at those points ('Records access restored...' R3-025, R3-032, R3-041, R3-049; 'Service junction restored...' R3-056, R3-099, R3-120). Knockdowns say 'Back at the last autosave.' (R3-070, R3-082, R3-108). The pause menu says 'Returning keeps your last checkpoint. Unsaved progress will be lost.' (R3-018).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The game uses three words (safe point, checkpoint, autosave) and teaches that only SAFE POINTs save, then saves silently in other places. The player can't predict how much progress a knockdown or Return to Title will cost, and 'the last autosave' points to something they never saw happen.
problems.suggestion: Use one word everywhere, for example 'checkpoint'. Show a small 'Checkpoint saved' toast or icon whenever an autosave happens. Change the title note to 'No checkpoint yet. Progress saves automatically as you go.' Make the knockdown line name the place, for example 'Back at the junction entrance.'

problems.title: The mirror hint still says 'examine the mirror port' after the mirror is copied
problems.what_player_sees: Right after choosing a mirror option, the station label reads MIRROR COPIED and the objective card reads REACH EXIT. The hint bar still says 'E: examine the mirror port.' (R1-033, R2-025, R3-038, R4-025). After Continue from the mirror save, the dialogue says 'Both traces are copied; head for the exit.' while the hint still says 'E: examine the mirror port.' (R3-041).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The hint contradicts the label above the object, the objective card and the dialogue in the same frame. It suggests there is still something to do at the mirror.
problems.suggestion: Refresh the hint as soon as the mirror trace is set, and after a restore. Use 'Both traces copied. Head for the exit.' and drop the E prompt at a copied station.

problems.title: The relay hint ignores what WOLF just said, and WOLF talks about the keyboard
problems.what_player_sees: Disclose route: WOLF says 'Thank you for telling me. I'll take the relay.' (R1-016). At the relay the hint still says 'E: ask WOLF to take the live relay.' (R1-019). Press route: WOLF says 'No. I won't take that risk blind. Use the bypass.' (R2-009, R3-009). At the relay the hint again says 'E: ask WOLF to take the live relay.' (R2-012, R3-012). Pressing it gets a second refusal that names a key: 'I said no... Press E again for the manual bypass.' (R2-013, R3-013).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The game offers to ask for something already agreed or already refused. The only way forward on the press route is to trigger a refusal you already heard. A character saying 'Press E' breaks the fiction and is wrong on a controller, where the button is A.
problems.suggestion: Base the relay hint on the earlier answer. After disclosure: 'E: signal WOLF to take the contact' (or start his walk automatically). After a refusal: 'E: take the manual bypass. WOLF refused the live contact.' straight away. Keep key names in the hint bar, never in WOLF's lines.

problems.title: 'WOLF holds the live contact' while the engineer is the one at the relay
problems.what_player_sees: R1-021/022/023: the text says 'WOLF holds the live contact by choice. Rowan keeps the breaker on.' In the picture the engineer stands in front of the COOLANT RELAY inside the coolant burst, WOLF stands behind him, and nobody is near the breaker. R2-014 (Rowan takes the bypass) looks almost the same: the engineer is at the relay and WOLF is beside him.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The text gives the roles the other way round from the picture. The key choice, WOLF taking the risk versus the engineer doing it, looks the same on screen, so the player can't see what the choice changed.
problems.suggestion: On the cooperate route, put WOLF at the relay contact with the coolant burst on him, and keep the engineer back or at the breaker as the text says. On the bypass route, keep the burst on the engineer. Or rewrite the line to match the staging.

problems.title: The relief vent goes off long before the 'top of the gauge'
problems.what_player_sees: The text says 'the relief vent lets go at the top of the gauge' and 'Move off it before the gauge peaks' (R3-068). In R3-069 the vent knocks the engineer down ('The relief vent let go under you. Stand clear of the grate when the gauge peaks.'). The dial over the valve is still at about 10 o'clock, far from its red zone. The same dial only reaches 12 o'clock when the seal is fully charged (R1-049), and never reaches red.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The game teaches 'wait for the peak', but the only gauge on screen is nowhere near its peak when the vent goes off. Players can't time the vent from what they're shown.
problems.suggestion: Give the vent its own readable warning, a meter or grate glow that ramps up and flashes just before it fires. Or rewrite the text to match the real rule ('the vent fires as the line builds; don't stand on the grate'). Make sure the dial and the text describe the same thing.

problems.title: 'The door blew' while the sealed door is still standing, and WOLF is unharmed in the blast spot
problems.what_player_sees: R3-081: 'The door blew with you in front of it.' The SEALED DOOR is still intact and labelled SEALED DOOR, the valve still reads SEAL CHARGED, and WOLF stands in the same spot as the engineer without being hurt. Earlier WOLF warned 'Don't stand in front of it when it goes' (R1-039) and then stood by the valve himself during every fuse (R1-049).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The knockdown cause isn't shown: no blast, no damaged door. The companion who gave the warning ignores it with no consequence.
problems.suggestion: Play the door blast, or at least a flash and debris, before the knockdown frame. Move WOLF left with the player when the fuse lights so he follows his own warning.

problems.title: The fuse hint sends the player across the glowing relief vent
problems.what_player_sees: R1-049: 'Fuse lit. Get left of the vent, away from the door.' The relief vent is glowing with a light column at that moment, and to get 'left of the vent' the engineer has to walk over the grate that knocked them down earlier.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: One hazard's safety instruction routes the player through the other hazard with no word on whether the vent is safe now.
problems.suggestion: Turn the vent visibly off once the seal is charged, and say so ('The vent is spent'). Or point the player at a landmark that isn't a hazard: 'Get back to the breaker.'

problems.title: WOLF 'will not cross' the rubble, then walks into the lane and stands under the tank
problems.what_player_sees: R1-050: 'WOLF holds at the rubble and will not cross.' After the player picks 'Draw it under the arm', WOLF walks well past the rubble to the sentry, nose to nose with it, with his head almost under the hanging tank (R1-058, R1-060), right after saying 'keep clear of the tank'.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The narration states a hard limit that WOLF breaks moments later. His own promise to keep clear of the tank doesn't match where he stands.
problems.suggestion: Change the narration to 'WOLF stops at the rubble' (no 'will not cross'), and have him stand clearly to one side of the floor mark when he holds the sentry.

problems.title: The ARM PANEL alcove both hides the player and gets them caught
problems.what_player_sees: R2-054: 'It lost you... The ARM PANEL alcove hides you from it.' The engineer is actually at the rubble, not in the alcove, and the sentry is parked inside the alcove next to the panel. R3-106: the engineer stands inside the alcove frame next to the panel and the game says 'The sentry's eyes snap red. It has you', then the knockdown (R3-107).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The game credits the alcove for a save that happened somewhere else, then catches the player while they appear to be in it. Where the alcove's cover actually starts and ends is never shown.
problems.suggestion: Draw the alcove's cover zone (floor shading or the frame lighting up while you're hidden), keep the sentry out of it, and base the 'lost you' line on where the player actually is ('The rubble broke its line of sight').

problems.title: 'E CONTINUE' at the end quietly returns to the title, and Continue then says the next part 'is not built yet'
problems.what_player_sees: R1-067: 'SERVICE LINE CLEARED... ROWAN: Then that's where we go.' with 'E CONTINUE'. Pressing it shows the title screen (R1-069) with no end-of-slice message. Continue drops the player back at the hatch: 'The hatch is open. The line beyond it is not built yet.' (R1-070, R1-072, R3-127, R3-129). Elsewhere 'E CONTINUE' just closes a dialogue line (R1-036).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The same prompt means 'next line' in one place and 'leave the game' in another. Continue lands the player at a dead end that breaks the fiction.
problems.suggestion: Show a clear end card, for example 'END OF CHAPTER 1 DEMO, progress saved', with 'E RETURN TO TITLE'. On the title, label Continue with the save point (for example 'Continue: Service Junction, cleared'), or offer New Game when the save is at the end of the demo.

problems.title: The Settings tab highlight stays on DISPLAY on every tab
problems.what_player_sees: The DISPLAY tab stays highlighted while the panel shows the Audio sliders (R3-063) and the Controls bindings (R3-064).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The selected-tab indicator doesn't match the content. Note: the driver switched tabs through signals, so this may be a focus highlight rather than a selection state, but it is what's on screen.
problems.suggestion: Draw the selected state from the active tab, apart from focus, and check it by clicking the tabs by hand.

problems.title: Settings show a window size that doesn't match the window, and sliders for audio that doesn't exist
problems.what_player_sees: WINDOW SIZE reads 960 × 540 while the game runs in a 1280×720 window (R3-061/062). Music and Voice volume sliders sit at 100%, and the note under them says 'there is no music or voice yet' (R3-063).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The settings report a state that isn't true, and they offer controls that do nothing.
problems.suggestion: Read the current window size into the dropdown when the panel opens. Hide or grey out the Music and Voice sliders until those sounds exist.

problems.title: WOLF refuses to draw the sentry with no reason tied to the earlier choice
problems.what_player_sees: R3-102/103: the same option that WOLF accepts in R1 ('Draw it under the arm if you can stay clear.') gets 'No. I won't walk into its sights.' The only difference is that the player pressed him at the relay much earlier. Nothing links the two.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: To the player the same request gets opposite answers at random. The memory system, the point of the choice, is invisible at the moment it matters.
problems.suggestion: Have WOLF name the reason: 'You sent me at the relay without a warning. I'm not walking into its sights on your word.' Or mark the option as unlikely to land before the player picks it.

problems.title: E at the breaker opens a relay conversation, and 'coolant fault' is never introduced
problems.what_player_sees: The objective is CHECK THE BREAKER and the player is at the BREAKER, but the hint is 'E: ask WOLF about the relay risk.' (R1-014). WOLF then says 'You know what 'coolant fault' means' (R1-015), though 'coolant fault' appears nowhere before, including on the optional purge display (R3-005).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The object's action doesn't match the object, and the dialogue refers to information the player was never given.
problems.suggestion: Make E at the breaker show a readout ('COOLANT FAULT: relay may vent when live'), then have WOLF ask. Or start the WOLF question at the relay, not the breaker.

problems.title: The red seal is still shut when the game says it's open, then it vanishes
problems.what_player_sees: R1-022 and R2-014: the hint says 'The seal is open. Move to the safe point.' and the text says 'the red seal rises', but the red seal door is still standing and glowing red. In R1-023/R1-024 it has disappeared with no frame or raised door left.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The state and the picture disagree for a beat, then the door pops out of existence instead of opening.
problems.suggestion: Animate the seal rising, turn its light green, and keep an open frame with an 'OPEN' label. Only show 'The seal is open' once it is visibly open.

problems.title: The Records exit says 'E: secure the first copy'
problems.what_player_sees: The objective is REACH EXIT and the player is at the red EXIT door, but the hint is 'E: secure the first copy.' (R1-035). Next the exit turns into a plain open frame, 'FIRST COPY SECURED' appears, and the hint becomes 'E: follow the service line toward Archive.' (R1-036/037).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The door's prompt names a data action that isn't a door's job, and the objective card says something else.
problems.suggestion: Put 'secure the copy' on a terminal by the exit, or make the exit prompt 'E: leave Records (secures the first copy)'. Line the objective card up with that.

problems.title: The Continue button doesn't say where it resumes, and New Game stays highlighted
problems.what_player_sees: Once a save exists, the title shows a bare CONTINUE with no note, while NEW GAME keeps the highlight (R1-069, R2-067, R4-059). Before any save there is a helpful note (R1-001).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: With autosaves possible at nine points, players can't tell what Continue will load. The default highlight invites an accidental New Game.
problems.suggestion: Add a note under Continue ('Service Junction: door down'), and focus Continue by default when a save exists.

problems.title: The clamp 'lets go' but the tank stays on a cable, and 'TANK DOWN' is labelled on the panel
