problems.what_player_sees: R1-061: 'The clamp lets go.' and 'The tank is falling.' while the tank still hangs in the clamp. R1-063/R1-072: after the crush the tank is still tied to the arm by a cable, and the alcove panel is relabelled 'TANK DOWN' instead of the tank.
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The text says it fell free but the picture shows it still tethered, and the state label sits on the wrong object.
problems.suggestion: Show the clamp opening and the tank falling free with no cable, put a 'TANK DOWN' or 'SENTRY DOWN' label over the mark, and keep the panel labelled 'ARM PANEL (spent)'.

problems.title: The objective card disappears during the tank drop
problems.what_player_sees: The top-left objective card (DROP THE TANK) disappears once the player enters the lane and stays gone through the drop (R1-056 to R1-061, R2-048 to R2-052, R3-104 to R3-106).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The goal display vanishes during the hardest, most confusing step.
problems.suggestion: Keep the objective card visible, shrunk if needed, throughout the lane sequence.

problems.title: Names for keys and objects don't match
problems.what_player_sees: The hint says 'HOLD E' and the dialogue says 'Hold USE' (R1-045/046). The same door is called 'EXIT BOLTED'/'EXIT BOLT'/'EXIT OPEN' on labels and 'the hatch' in hints and dialogue (R1-060, R1-064 to R1-066).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: Small mismatches make the player wonder whether these are different things.
problems.suggestion: Use the bound key name in every prompt, and one noun per object (for example 'HATCH' on the label too).

problems.title: Continuing from the junction entrance skips WOLF's move ahead
problems.what_player_sees: A fresh arrival has WOLF run ahead and say 'It's live. Don't stand in front of it when it goes.' (R1-038/039). After Continue from the junction entrance save, WOLF starts behind the engineer at the far left and that beat never plays (R3-056/057).
problems.why_it_makes_no_sense: The restored scene doesn't match what the player saw before, and the only blast warning is lost on a retry.
problems.suggestion: After a restore at the entrance, replay WOLF's walk and warning line, or fold the warning into the 'Service junction restored' text.

what_works: Pause really freezes the world: the line gauge reads 0.11 in every Pause and Settings shot (R3-060 to R3-065) and picks up again at 0.13 after resume (R3-066).

Continue from each save restores the right objective card and a short line fitted to that save ('Records access restored. The purge order is copied; copy the mirror index next.', 'Service junction restored. The sentry is down; pop the exit bolt by the hatch.'): R3-020, R3-025, R3-032, R3-049, R3-099, R3-120, R3-127.

Knockdown messages name the cause and tell the player what to do differently (vent R3-069, blast R3-081, sentry R3-107), and the scene resets cleanly. Breaker labels go back to OVERLOAD BREAKER and the objective goes back to CLEAR THE LINE (R3-070, R3-082).

Object labels follow state through the junction: OVERLOAD BREAKER, then BREAKER LIVE, BREAKER TRIPPED and BREAKER SPENT. Likewise VALVE 0/3 to SEAL CHARGED to VALVE SPENT, SEALED DOOR to DOOR DOWN, ARM PANEL to ARM REWINDING, and EXIT BOLTED to EXIT OPEN.
The valve turn count matches across the hint, the dialogue and the label (R1-045 to R1-048), and the three green lights fill as it charges.
Before any save, the title's Continue button is disabled with a clear reason (R1-001), and it is enabled after a save (R1-069).
The Pause menu warns that Return to Title keeps the last checkpoint and loses unsaved progress (R3-018).
WOLF's safe-point line remembers the player's exact words and what followed, and it differs by route (R1-025, R2-017, R4-017). The Records greeting changes too (R1-026, R2-018, R4-018).
After a miss, the winch re-arm is explained ('The winch has the tank back on the clamp. The ARM PANEL is ready again.' R2-055), so recovery is possible without a knockdown.
The engineer-only fallback works: a refusal at the relay or in the lane still leaves a manual path to the full clear (R2, R3).

syn.summary_plain: The four reviews agree that the worst problems are in the Service Junction. The tank drop and the panel alcove are the two places where you have to read the screen to survive, and in both the code tests something other than what is drawn. The hit check looks only at the sentry's centre, and a baited sentry keeps moving while the tank falls. The hidden zone is narrower than the drawn frame. After a miss, the sentry drives straight through the tank lying on the floor. Several hints and lines don't follow the game's own state: the relay hint ignores WOLF's answer, the mirror hint goes stale, "get left of the vent" points the wrong way, and "the seal is open" shows before it opens. These are plain defects with small fixes. The story problems need Nathanial: Rowan is never introduced, the purge stakes only appear on an optional display, the bypass costs nothing, and WOLF's refusals never give a reason. Evidence here is driven-play screenshots plus logged positions, not hands-on play.

problems.title: Whether the tank hits or misses doesn't match what the screen shows
problems.what_player_sees: R2: the drop is called a miss, then the next frame shows the sentry right under the tank, which is still sitting on the floor in the coolant cloud. R4: the tank is let go while the sentry is about 110 px right of the mark (WOLF hasn't reached the lane yet), and it is still 'comes down square and crushes the sentry flat'. The sentry also jumps onto the mark at impact. WOLF said 'Drop it when it stops', but the R4 drop came before it stopped and still won.
problems.why: This is the main action of the encounter, and a player learns its timing from what they see. Here a drop that looks on target misses, and a drop that looks off target hits. Players will call the miss a bug and the hit luck.
evidence: R2-052-miss-cloud-and-alert.png (sentry_x 701.8, chasing, passing under the tank that is still on the floor)
R4-048-hint-e-drop-the-tank-it-lands.png (sentry 812 patrol, WOLF 530 not yet in the lane)
R4-049-dialogue-the-clamp-lets-go.png / R4-050-sentry-fixated.png (sentry fixated and moving 786 to 759 during the fall)
R1-055 / R4-047 'Drop it when it stops'
problems.root_cause: There are four causes. (1) DropArm.is_hit() (scripts/drop_arm.gd) checks the sentry's centre against MARK_X±44, but the brackets are drawn ±44 (junction_room.gd:878) and the sentry body is ±26 wide. A sentry whose body is visibly inside the brackets can still miss. (2) main.gd _tick_lane ticks sentry_brain before drop_arm.advance on every frame of the 0.45 s fall. Once WOLF crosses LANE_ENTRY_X mid-fall, the sentry switches to fixated and moves at CHASE_SPEED 230 px/s toward WOLF_BAIT_X+64 = 700, about 100 px during the fall, so an early drop gets pulled into a hit. _tank_hit() then sets sentry_brain.x = MARK_X, which is the visible snap. (3) After a miss, DropArm.drop_amount() during rewinding is rewind_remaining/REWIND_SECONDS, so the tank starts on the floor and takes 6 s to rise. Meanwhile sentry_brain.alert() starts a chase that drives the sentry straight through the tank's floor position. (4) Nothing makes the drop wait for 'when it stops': _drop_ready() and _use_arm_panel() allow the drop as soon as the tank is hung.
problems.minimal_fix: 1. Make one rule the brackets show: a hit means the sentry's body overlaps the brackets at landing. In is_hit, use HIT_RANGE + SentryBrain.HALF_WIDTH, or keep the test and narrow the drawn brackets to match. 2. While WOLF is baiting, accept the drop only once sentry_brain.state == &"fixated" and the sentry has reached its hold point. Before that the panel says 'Wait. WOLF hasn't got it on the mark yet.' This makes 'Drop it when it stops' true and removes the mid-fall pull-in. 3. On a miss, lift the tank to its hanging height within the first ~0.3 s of the rewind (an ease-out curve in drop_amount), so the chasing sentry never drives through a tank still on the floor. 4. With rule 1 in place the snap to MARK_X shrinks to a few px. Update tests/sentry_test.gd and tests/junction_test.gd for the new hit range and drop gate.

problems.title: The panel alcove is called the safe spot, but you get spotted and run down inside its drawn frame
problems.what_player_sees: Standing at the ARM PANEL inside the drawn alcove frame still gives 'You're in its lane. Get into the panel alcove'. In R3 the engineer stands inside the frame, just right of the panel, when 'The sentry's eyes snap red', and is run down there. In R2, after a miss, the game says 'The ARM PANEL alcove hides you from it' while the engineer is back on the rubble and the sentry is parked inside the alcove frame.
problems.why: Where to stand is the one rule of this encounter, and the frame is the only cue for it. Being told you are exposed inside the frame, then killed there, makes the failure feel unfair and the rule impossible to learn.
evidence: R1-059-hint-you-re-in-its-lane-get.png and R2-048 (engineer_x 550.5: inside the frame, outside COVER_MIN_X 556)
R3-106-dialogue-the-sentry-s-eyes-snap-red.png (engineer_x 588.7: inside the frame, 4.7 px past COVER_MAX_X 584)
R2-054-dialogue-it-lost-you-and-goes-back.png (engineer_x 499.8 on the rubble, sentry_x 600 inside the frame)
problems.root_cause: In scripts/sentry_brain.gd the hidden zone is the engineer's centre between COVER_MIN_X 556 and COVER_MAX_X 584, only 28 px. junction_room.gd:767 draws the frame wider by HUMAN_HALF_WIDTH on each side (542 to 598). A sprite that looks well inside the frame can therefore be exposed, and there is an exposed 11 px gap between LANE_ENTRY_X 545 and 556. CHASE_MIN_X is 586, so a chase can park the sentry inside the frame, and after a lost chase it walks back to PATROL_MIN_X 624 at patrol speed from there. main.gd:1529 always prints 'The ARM PANEL alcove hides you', but a chase is only ever lost when the engineer is at x <= LANE_ENTRY_X, which is the rubble, not the alcove.
problems.minimal_fix: Set the hidden zone to the drawn frame: COVER_MIN_X = LANE_ENTRY_X (545) and COVER_MAX_X = 598, and draw the frame from those two values with no extra half-width added. PATROL_MIN_X then follows automatically (598+40). Change the lose line in _sentry_changed to 'It lost you behind the rubble and goes back to its patrol.' Optionally tint the alcove floor so the safe floor reads as a different surface. Update tests/sentry_test.gd constants.

problems.title: The relay hint ignores what WOLF just said, and WOLF talks like a button prompt
problems.what_player_sees: Press route: WOLF says 'No. I won't take that risk blind. Use the bypass.' At the relay the hint still says 'E: ask WOLF to take the live relay.', and pressing it gets 'I said no... Press E again for the manual bypass.' Disclose route: WOLF has already said 'I'll take the relay', and the hint still asks the player to ask him.
problems.why: You have to repeat a request WOLF already refused, which makes the engineer look like they ignored him and makes WOLF feel like a menu. A key name in WOLF's voice breaks the fiction. All four reviews flagged this.
problems.root_cause: main.gd _context_hint (around line 2112) and _interact_relay (around line 1089) branch on the local flag relay_refused. That flag is only set after the relay itself returns "refused", so WOLF's refusal at the breaker (memory choice_id == PRESS) is ignored until a second press triggers a second refusal. The disclose route reuses the same 'ask WOLF' hint text. main.gd:1106 hard-codes 'Press E again...' into WOLF's line; _set_dialogue rewrites the key but it is still a UI instruction in his voice.
problems.minimal_fix: In _interact_relay and _context_hint, treat state.memory.get("choice_id") == M0State.PRESS the same as relay_refused. The first E at the relay then runs the human bypass, and the hint reads 'E: take the manual bypass. WOLF refused the live contact.' On the disclose route, change the hint to 'E: signal WOLF to take the contact.' Delete 'Press E again for the manual bypass.' from WOLF's line; it becomes unreachable.

problems.title: 'Get left of the vent' sends you across the vent, and the blast knockdown never shows the door blowing
problems.what_player_sees: SEAL CHARGED gives 'Get left of the vent before the fuse ends.' The engineer is at the valve, and the only way left is over the relief vent they were just warned off. Staying put gives 'The door blew with you in front of it.' over a frame where the door is still intact and labelled SEALED DOOR. WOLF stands at the valve or in the steam the whole time and is never hurt, even after his own warning 'Don't stand in front of it when it goes.'
problems.why: The instruction points into a hazard and further than needed, and the failure has no visible cause. Their companion standing in the same spot unharmed makes the danger look arbitrary.
problems.root_cause: In scripts/pressure_line.gd the blast zone is BLAST_MIN_X 360 to BLAST_MAX_X 540, and VALVE_X 420 sits inside it. The vent (250 to 350) only hurts while the line is 'building', so once the seal is charged anywhere left of 360 is safe. main.gd lines 1303/1315/1647/2140 and JunctionRoom.BLAST_REASON all name the wrong landmark ('left of the vent'). In main.gd _door_blast(), when the engineer is in the zone the code calls _fail_beat() before junction_room.door_blast(), so the door art never changes. _wolf_target_x() has no case for a charged or lit fuse, so WOLF keeps following the engineer into the zone, or stays at WOLF_SEAM_X 418, which is inside it.
problems.minimal_fix: Change the four lines and BLAST_REASON to 'Back away from the door, past the valve' / 'Fuse lit. Get clear of the door.' Paint hazard stripes on the floor from 360 to 540 that pulse while pressure_line.is_dangerous(). In the fail branch of _door_blast, play the blast burst and the blown-door art before _fail_beat; the autosave restore brings the sealed door back. In _wolf_target_x, when pressure_line.is_dangerous(), send WOLF to about x 320, which is outside the zone with the vent already quiet.

problems.title: The relief vent rule can't be read: it steams the whole build and the gauge reads empty when it hits you
problems.what_player_sees: 'The relief vent lets go at the top of the gauge.' A steam column comes off the vent from the moment the line starts building. None of the dials is labelled as the line gauge. In the knockdown frame the valve's dial needle is back at empty, so it looks as if the vent went off long before the peak. WOLF stands on the grate unharmed.
problems.why: Safe steam and deadly steam look the same, and the one gauge the player is told to watch shows 'empty' at the moment of failure, so the knockdown feels random.
problems.root_cause: In junction_room.gd sync_line (around lines 525 to 528), vent_steam emits for the whole 'building' state, from gauge 0 at 0.3 alpha. PressureLine.advance() sets gauge = 0.0 on the same frame it trips, while the grate stays dangerous for HAZARD_SECONDS 0.4. The knockdown frame therefore draws the needle at empty. The gauge is the needle drawn over the valve's painted dial (_draw_gauge_and_lights) and has no label. WOLF follows the engineer and has no hazard check.
problems.minimal_fix: Emit vent steam only above gauge ~0.6, and add a hard warning (flash or hiss spike) from ~0.85. Keep the drawn needle pinned at full, in red, through the HAZARD_SECONDS window and the knockdown, for example a separate display_gauge in JunctionRoom that eases back to 0 only after the trip. Add a small 'LINE' caption to the dial. Keep WOLF's target off the grate while the line is building.

problems.title: The relay payoff text describes a scene that isn't on screen, and 'the seal is open' shows before it opens
problems.what_player_sees: 'WOLF holds the live contact by choice. Rowan keeps the breaker on; the red seal rises.' On screen Rowan stands in the coolant relay, nobody is near the breaker, and WOLF lets go and walks away almost at once. The hint 'The seal is open. Move to the safe point.' shows while the seal is still fully shut. The seal is a free-standing pillar with no wall around it, and it shrinks away instead of rising. The cooperate and bypass routes look almost identical.
problems.why: The player can't connect their choice to the result when the result is announced before it is shown, the roles are swapped, and both branches are staged the same.
evidence: R1-021-wolf-to-592-arrived.png (engineer_x 603 at the relay; WOLF reaches 592 and immediately follows)
problems.root_cause: main.gd _wolf_takes_relay() sets wolf_heading_to_relay = false on arrival, so _wolf_target_x() returns -1 and WOLF goes straight back to following. The engineer has to press E within ±52 of the relay at x 605, which overlaps RELAY_CONTACT_X 592, so both actors stand in the relay. The line at main.gd:1110/1130 hard-codes 'keeps the breaker on'. state.door_open becomes true at once, so _context_hint (line 2100) shows 'The seal is open' while _sync_door's 0.38 s tween is still running. That tween collapses scale:y to 0 instead of sliding the seal up. The seal has no surrounding frame art.
problems.minimal_fix: Keep WOLF at RELAY_CONTACT_X until the door tween finishes (or until the engineer reaches the safe point), and step the engineer back from the relay before the line plays. Rewrite the line: 'WOLF takes the surge through the live contact; the red seal grinds upward.' Hint 'The seal is opening.' while door_tween is running and 'is open' after. Tween position.y upward into a header instead of scale:y. A bulkhead frame around the seal needs new art.

problems.title: The mirror hint still says 'examine the mirror port' after the copy
problems.what_player_sees: The station reads MIRROR COPIED and the card reads REACH EXIT, but the hint still says 'E: examine the mirror port.' After Continue from the mirror save the dialogue says 'Both traces are copied; head for the exit' over the same stale hint.
problems.why: The hint contradicts the label, the objective and the dialogue in the same frame, so the player may keep pressing E or think the copy failed.
problems.root_cause: main.gd _context_hint around line 2091: the mirror branch checks only state.purge_trace_preserved and never mirror_trace_preserved. The purge branch above it has the 'already copied' case; the mirror branch doesn't.
problems.minimal_fix: Change it to: if state.mirror_trace_preserved: return "Mirror copied. Head for the exit." before the existing line.

problems.title: WOLF says he'll keep clear of the tank, then stands under it
problems.what_player_sees: 'I'll draw it onto the mark and keep clear of the tank.' WOLF's body then sits inside the floor brackets under the hanging tank, nose to nose with the sentry, and the clamp lets go with him there.
problems.why: The line and the picture disagree, and a player who cares about WOLF will hold off dropping. The drop then doesn't hurt him, which teaches that the tank only hurts sentries.
problems.root_cause: JunctionRoom.WOLF_BAIT_X = MARK_X - SentryBrain.BAIT_OFFSET (64) puts WOLF at 636 with a logic body of ±31 (M0State.WOLF_HALF_WIDTH). His drawn sprite is about 150 world px wide, so his head reaches the bracket and the tank's footprint. The spacing was tuned to the 62 px logic body, not the art.
problems.minimal_fix: Increase BAIT_OFFSET, or set WOLF_BAIT_X directly, so the sprite's front edge stops outside the bracket: about MARK_X - HIT_RANGE - 80, roughly x 575 to 580. Or flip WOLF to face the sentry from beyond the right edge. Re-check the post-miss backing-off margin noted in the BAIT_OFFSET comment.

problems.title: The relay risk has no stakes: the bypass is the same box, costs nothing, and the 'coolant fault' never shows up
problems.what_player_sees: WOLF quotes 'coolant fault' before anything has shown one. The hint says 'ask WOLF about the relay risk', but WOLF asks you. The 'manual bypass' is the same COOLANT RELAY box, free and instant, and no coolant ever vents on any route. In R4 the engineer overrides WOLF after he volunteered, and he answers only 'I stayed with you.' 'We can talk after' is quoted but never followed up.
problems.why: The choice is set up as a real risk with nothing behind it. If a safe, free bypass exists, asking WOLF to touch a live contact makes the engineer look careless, and WOLF's refusal or courage means little.
evidence: R2-014 / R4-013 / R4-014 (bypass on the same box)
problems.root_cause: Design or content. In M0State.activate_power("human"), route 'fallback' has no condition or cost. Nothing in the corridor draws a coolant fault. main.gd:1061 quotes the phrase. No branch ever vents coolant.
problems.minimal_fix: Decide what the bypass costs (slower hold-to-crank, a coolant puff the engineer steps back from, an alarm) and give it its own labelled MANUAL BYPASS handle. Put a visible COOLANT FAULT tag on the relay. Change the breaker hint to 'E: talk to WOLF about the relay.' Add an R4-specific safe-point line and an optional 'You said we'd talk after' beat.

problems.title: Why you're in Records is only explained on an optional display
problems.what_player_sees: The only line that states the goal ('Original program logs marked for deletion... We need to preserve it.') is behind 'READ DISPLAY (optional)'. Skip it and you get 'the original logs', 'purge order... target ID', 'The purge target existed before the deletion order', 'A list doesn't tell me who's a threat' and 'Archive is next', none of which have been set up.
problems.why: Every Records objective depends on stakes the main path never states. The mirror 'finding' reads as a tautology, and 'the list' refers to nothing on screen.
problems.root_cause: Content. main.gd:1045 shows the purge explanation only when the player presses E at x <= 230, and the tutorial labels it optional (_refresh_ui). The later Records lines assume it was read.
problems.minimal_fix: Have WOLF or Rowan speak the one core line on entering the corridor or passing the display. Give the mirror result one line of meaning, such as 'flagged before any incident, so this is a cover-up'. Replace 'A list' with what was actually copied, and name Archive earlier.

problems.title: Rowan, the playable engineer, is never introduced, and the narration speaks about him in the third person
problems.what_player_sees: The opening shows only the Director and WOLF. The engineer first appears already standing beside WOLF in the corridor, named only by a 'ROWAN:' line. WOLF retells events Rowan supposedly wasn't there for, and Rowan signs on in one line. After that the narration says 'Rowan takes the bypass', 'Rowan keeps the breaker on'.
problems.why: The player isn't told who they are, why they're here, or why they would trust a military robot that just broke out. Third-person narration also blurs whether Rowan is 'you'.
problems.root_cause: Story staging. The intro sequence (main.gd _advance_intro) never places the engineer, and _finish_intro cuts straight to a corridor with both actors present. The narration lines use state.human_name() in the third person.
problems.minimal_fix: Add one beat or name card when control starts ('ROWAN / MAINTENANCE ENGINEER') with a one-line reason to trust WOLF, and choose either 'You' or a third-person voice set up from the start.

problems.title: Narration appears under the Director's name tag
problems.what_player_sees: Under DIRECTOR: 'He thinks WOLF is still in standby.' and 'WOLF turns from him and takes the only open route.' Other beats use inline 'DIRECTOR: / WOLF:', and others mix narration and speech in one box.
problems.why: It reads as if the antagonist is narrating himself, and the format keeps changing who is talking.
problems.root_cause: main.gd _set_dialogue (around lines 2038 to 2047) tags the whole box with the first line's speaker whenever the second line does not begin with a named speaker. The narration second lines at main.gd:503 and :547 therefore fall under DIRECTOR.
problems.minimal_fix: Tag the box only when every line belongs to that speaker, for example when there is no second line or the second line has the same speaker. Otherwise show it untagged with the inline 'DIRECTOR:' name, the same format the other multi-speaker beats use. Better still, split the two intro lines into separate beats.

problems.title: WOLF 'will not cross' the rubble, then crosses it, and his yes or no to baiting looks random
problems.what_player_sees: 'WOLF holds at the rubble and will not cross.' Seconds later, if you ask, he walks into the lane under the tank. In another run the same polite request gets 'No. I won't walk into its sights' with no reason given.
problems.why: The narration states a firm rule that a branch then breaks. Because the cause of his choice (how you handled the relay) is never mentioned, his trust looks arbitrary rather than a response to you.
problems.root_cause: main.gd:1688 hard-codes 'will not cross'. M0State.wolf_will_bait() returns memory choice_id == DISCLOSE, so the yes or no is decided by the relay choice, but neither line in _choose_lane mentions it.
problems.minimal_fix: Change the line to 'WOLF stops at the rubble and waits for your call.' Add one clause to each baiting answer tying it to the relay, for example 'You told me the truth at the relay. I'll draw it.' and 'Last time you sent me in blind. Time it from the panel.'

problems.title: The junction's sealed door sits in the back wall and never blocks the lane
problems.what_player_sees: The SEALED DOOR faces the camera in the back wall, and the ARM PANEL, the tank and the lit floor beyond are visible and look walkable before the blast. The blown hole shows more wall. The engineer walks along the floor past the frame, not through it. The sentry then appears 'from the dark past the door' in an area that was visibly lit and empty.
problems.why: A door in the back wall can't stop sideways walking, so the whole breaker, valve and blast sequence looks like it unlocks nothing. The sentry seems to appear from thin air.
problems.root_cause: Level and art layout. M0State blocks movement at JUNCTION_DOOR_LEFT_X with an invisible limit while the door is drawn as a back-wall prop (JunctionRoom.DOOR_X 480). The lane past it is drawn and lit before the blast, and SentryBrain starts 'dormant' at PATROL_MAX_X with no visual dormant state.
problems.minimal_fix: Either make the door a side-on bulkhead across the lane, or darken or hide everything past x 540 until door_blown and show the sentry dormant (eyes dark) in a recess. This needs an art decision.

problems.title: Autosaves happen silently, but the title says only safe points save
problems.what_player_sees: The title says 'No checkpoint yet. Reach a SAFE POINT to save.' Only the corridor safe point ever says 'saved'. Later, knockdowns say 'Back at the last autosave' and Continue resumes from several Records and junction stages the player never saw being saved.
problems.why: Three terms (safe point, checkpoint, autosave) and hidden saves leave the player unsure what a knockdown or Return to Title will cost.
problems.root_cause: main.gd _save_progress() writes without any feedback (lines 1149 to 1690 call it at every beat), and NO_CHECKPOINT_NOTE (main.gd:15) describes only safe points.
problems.minimal_fix: Show a small 'Checkpoint saved' toast in _save_progress (the top card or the hint bar) when the save succeeds. Change NO_CHECKPOINT_NOTE to 'Progress saves at safe points and checkpoints.' Use 'checkpoint' everywhere.

problems.title: Continue from junction save A skips WOLF's blast warning and starts him clipped into the wall
problems.what_player_sees: A fresh entry plays WOLF running ahead and 'It's live. Don't stand in front of it when it goes.' Continue from save A, and the knockdown restores, start WOLF at the far left, half off-screen over the vault door, with only 'Service junction restored...'.
problems.why: A continuing player never hears the one warning about the blast, so the blast knockdown feels unfair. The companion half inside a wall looks broken.
problems.root_cause: M0State.enter_junction() saves wolf_position (64, 423). His sprite is about 150 px wide, so at x 64 it overhangs the room edge. The restore path (main.gd around line 1003) sets wolf_scouting = false and the junction restore line (line 1018) leaves out the warning.
problems.minimal_fix: Start WOLF at x of at least 90, beside the engineer. On restore in the idle junction state, either re-run the scouting walk (wolf_scouting = true) or add 'WOLF: Don't stand in front of the door when it goes.' to the restore line.

problems.title: The slice ends by cutting to the title, and Continue leads to a 'not built yet' dead end
problems.what_player_sees: After 'SERVICE LINE CLEARED... Then that's where we go.' the game cuts to the title with no end card. Continue puts you back in the junction with 'The hatch is open. The line beyond it is not built yet.'
problems.why: The cut can look like a crash or a reset, and a developer note in the game's voice reads like a bug.
problems.root_cause: main.gd _leave_junction() goes from the chapter close straight back to the title. The cleared state's text is at main.gd:1371 and :2160.
problems.minimal_fix: Add an 'END OF SLICE / thanks for playing' card, optionally with a recap of the player's choices, before the title. When junction_cleared, set the title's Continue note to 'Slice complete' and move the 'not built yet' text out of the dialogue box.

problems.title: Exits and data stations don't read as doors or terminals
problems.what_player_sees: You 'secure the first copy' at the red EXIT door, which stays red, then turns into a flat navy box. The junction hatch says 'The hatch slides open' while the sprite is still closed, then becomes a flat teal box. The corridor moves to Records through a solid wall with no doorway.
problems.why: Securing data at a door makes no sense, and an opened door that leads to a blank panel, or that text says is open while it is shut, breaks cause and effect.
problems.root_cause: records_room.gd _draw_exit() draws flat placeholder rectangles for the open doorway, and the 'secure' action is bound to the exit station at x 830. main.gd _bolt_arc() prints 'slides open' HATCH_OPEN_SECONDS before the hatch tween starts. The corridor has no RECORDS door prop.
problems.minimal_fix: Plain part: move 'The hatch slides open' to when the hatch tween finishes. Art and station part: add an UPLINK terminal for the secure action, open-state door art with a lit passage, and a RECORDS door in the corridor. These need new assets and asset-register entries.

problems.title: The exit bolt runs on a 'spare overload' from a breaker labelled SPENT
problems.what_player_sees: The breaker reads BREAKER SPENT after the blast, then 'The spare overload runs into the exit bolt.'
problems.why: The game just taught that the overload was used on the door. A spare one nobody mentioned undercuts that.
problems.root_cause: Copy at main.gd:1387 (_pop_bolt), with no drawn power line to the bolt panel.
problems.minimal_fix: Rewrite as, for example, 'With the tank down, the arm's feed reroutes into the exit bolt. The panel whines.' and extend the schematic line to the bolt panel.

problems.title: In the opening WOLF leaves left, back toward his cage, and the cage bars just vanish
problems.what_player_sees: 'The gate slides aside', but the bars disappear. 'WOLF turns from him and takes the only open route' while WOLF walks left toward the cage he just left, and the scene cuts.
problems.why: No exit is shown, and the movement reads as WOLF going back in.
problems.root_cause: main.gd _advance_intro: step 4 sets wolf.autonomous_target_x = 110 (left, toward the cage), and step 2 tweens intro_gate 'opening' then calls intro_gate.hide().
problems.minimal_fix: Send WOLF right, past the Director, toward a visible maintenance door, and leave the gate drawn in its open position instead of hiding it. This is a staging decision.

problems.title: Objectives and labels use confusing or premature words
problems.what_player_sees: 'DROP THE TANK' appears the moment the door blows, before the tank is mentioned. 'ARM PANEL' sits in a room where 'arm' is also the breaker verb. 'Arm the breaker on the left' is said while you stand left of it. The junction door is called a 'seal'. 'CORRIDOR CLEARED' names nothing. 'Hold USE' in dialogue vs 'HOLD E' in the hint. 'WOLF brings the mirror timestamp by his own choice' right after the player picked it. 'I'm checking this path too' is vague.
problems.why: Each one is small, but together they make a newcomer stop to decode words instead of acting.
problems.root_cause: Copy in main.gd _objective() (around lines 2193 to 2220), _junction_hint 'on the left' strings, _interact_junction 'Hold USE' (line 1313), and JunctionRoom arm_label 'ARM PANEL' (line 317).
problems.minimal_fix: 'ARM PANEL' to 'TANK RELEASE'. 'on the left' to 'by the entrance'. Show 'Hold E' through the same prompt substitution _set_dialogue uses for 'Press E'. 'CORRIDOR CLEARED' to 'SAFE POINT REACHED'. Show DROP THE TANK only after the first lane line. 'blast door' instead of 'seal' in the junction. The mirror and Records lines are WOLF's voice, so check those with Nathanial.

problems.title: Tank and arm state details contradict themselves
problems.what_player_sees: A tank that 'vents coolant' on a miss is winched up and reused intact. A tank 'released' by the clamp is still drawn on a cable. TANK DOWN floats over the panel, not the tank. The ARM PANEL uses the same lever-box sprite as both breakers, with no line up to the arm.
problems.why: Small breaks that make the release mechanism harder to read.
problems.root_cause: junction_room.gd draws the cable from cable_top to tank_top in every state (around lines 852 to 873). arm_label carries the TANK DOWN text (line 618). _tank_miss text says the tank 'vents coolant'.
problems.minimal_fix: Stop drawing the cable while falling or landed, or call it a winch cable that pays out. Move the TANK DOWN label to the tank. Reword the miss as 'dents and sprays coolant from a split line'. A distinct release-lever sprite needs art.

problems.title: The engineer is drawn inside machines
problems.what_player_sees: Rowan stands inside the coolant relay and the mirror port, and only his head shows behind the purge queue.
problems.why: It is unclear where the player is standing.
problems.root_cause: The use ranges are centred on the station (±52 or ±58 of x), so the engineer stops in the middle of the prop, and the station props sit at actor depth.
problems.minimal_fix: Draw the actors in front of the station props, or offset each use range so the engineer stands beside the machine.

problems.title: Settings tab highlight stuck on DISPLAY (capture artifact, not a game defect)
problems.what_player_sees: The Audio and Controls pages appear with the DISPLAY tab still highlighted.
problems.why: Listed for completeness. The capture driver caused it, not the game.
problems.root_cause: logic-audit/game/review_capture/routes.gd:189 called menu.select_tab(i) directly. In the game, select_tab only runs from TabBar.tab_changed (game_settings.gd:148), and that already moves the highlight.
problems.minimal_fix: Nothing is needed. For safety, select_tab could also set tabs.current_tab = index. Confirm with one mouse and one controller check.

what_works: World labels change state with every action (BREAKER to LIVE to SPENT, VALVE 0/3 to SEAL CHARGED, SEALED DOOR to DOOR DOWN, ARM PANEL to ARM REWINDING to TANK DOWN, EXIT BOLTED to OPEN, PURGE and MIRROR COPIED), so cause and effect can be read from the labels alone (R1-043, R1-050, R2-051, R1-066).
The objective card moves one step at a time and nearly always names the next interaction.
The valve crank gives feedback in three places at once: the hint ('1 of 3 turns'), the dialogue, and the three-light meter going green (R1-047 to R1-049).
The junction's drawn schematic line from the breaker to the vent, valve and door shows what feeds what, and on a vent trip the whole line turns red (R1-038, R3-069).
Knockdowns name the cause and the fix, then restore quickly to the start of the current puzzle (R3-069/070, R3-107/108).
The missed-drop loop reads as a sequence: cloud, chase, 'stay back over the rubble', lost, re-armed (R2-051 to R2-055). Only the hit test and the alcove geometry need fixing.
WOLF reads as his own character. He agrees when told the truth and refuses when rushed, and the safe point quotes the player's exact words back to them on every route (R1-025, R2-017, R4-017).
Every WOLF-dependent step has a working engineer-only fallback: manual bypass, manual mirror port, timed drop (R2-013/014, R2-025, R2-060).
The self-awakening opening and the Director's aim ('I decide who counts as a threat. WOLF handles the rest.') are clear and chilling (R1-002 to R1-008).
Continue from every save restores the right objective with a one-line 'restored' summary. Pause freezes the line, with the gauge holding at 0.11 (R3-060 to R3-065).
The art reads well at 1280x720: big station labels, clear floor-mark brackets and a visible alcove frame. The logic just has to match them.
questions_for_user: Relay bypass: what should it cost so that asking WOLF means something? Options are slower hold-to-crank, a coolant hit the engineer steps back from, an alarm, or a longer route. Should it be a separate MANUAL BYPASS handle rather than the same relay box?
Should WOLF's yes or no to baiting the sentry openly name the earlier relay choice ('You told me the truth at the relay'), or stay unspoken on purpose?
